items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Eddie Durham had left Jimmy Lunceford and joined us in '37

ctx.x: That makes for a brass section -
But prior to that time before we added Benny Morton in '37, Eddie Durham had left Jimmy Lunceford and joined us in '37...
What did he join you as, a trombone player?

items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: Joe Turner would sing and Jo Jones would have his snare drum, he'd come in -- no, with his sock cymbal, and it'd be about three of us.

ctx.x: Then I'd go there and I'd jump up on the stage there and sit up on the bar and get the guitar, and Joe Turner would wipe his hands, and he'd come there and he'd sing, see, and Joe Turner would sing and Jo Jones would have his snare drum, he'd come in -- no, with his sock cymbal, and it'd be about three of us. And that was another job. We used to work there until about 7:00 the next morning.

And he didn't have to pay us anything, because when I'd come out, money'd be sticking all up -- rolled up and stuck into the guitar, and put it in Joe Turner's pocket and that's where I first met him, and we used to play like that.
